newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Issuers look afield for funds.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Issuers look afield for funds.

text.p: Thursday offered what has become a typical scenario for Asian debt markets, with an Asian borrower tapping investors outside Asia and a non-Asian borrower looking to Asia for funding.
Thailand's Total Access Communications launched a two-tranche US$400 million 144a bond in New York overnight via lead manager UBS Securities.
The US$300 million 8.375 percent 10-year bond was priced to yield 8.409 percent, or 200 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
The US$100 million 7.625 percent five-year tranche was priced to yield 7.632 percent, or 150 basis points over the benchmark.
TAC has a split rating, assessed at Ba1 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB-minus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
Pricing was in line with expectations.
The bond was the biggest deal ever for a Thai corporate and the largest Yankee bond for an Asian issuer, a manager at UBS pointed out.
UBS said the deal was well received despite economic and political uncertainty in Thailand and soft market for emerging market debt generally.
For example, Brazil's US$750 million five-year global bond that launched on Monday has weakened in the secondary market, reportedly trading at 99.375/99.875.
Traders in Hong Kong noted, however, that Asian debt tends to get a better reception than other emerging market deals.
In other news, the 10-year Yankee bond for South Korea's Pohang Iron and Steel was trading at 69-70 basis points over Treasuries, right where it priced.

In Europe, AAA-rated Deutsche Pfandbrief- Und Hypothekenbank launched a 1.0 billion mark Euro-Asian bond. The five-year bond will be priced later today to yield 5-7 basis points over German government bunds.
The bonds are listed in Frankfurt and Singapore. Coordinator Morgan Stanley said it expects good demand in Asia.
Pfandbrief bonds are mortgage bonds issued by mortgage banks in Germany and secured by their mortgage lendings.

Closer to home, Union Bank of Switzerland Hong Kong branch launched a fixed-rate HK$500 million five-year deal that carries a coupon of 7.38 percent payable semi-annually. It was priced to yield 7.54 percent to maturity and 7.56 percent to a call option at the third anniversary. UBS was the lead.
Union Bank of Bangkok launched a US$20 million subordinated floating rate note through KDB Asia.
Korea Development Bank is scheduled to roadshow its US$500 million global bond in Hong Kong on Friday, bankers said. Merrill Lynch and JP Morgan are the leads.
Looking further ahead, Thailand said it plans to issue two samurais worth a total of 30 billion yen during in November or December to raise funds for Thai Airways International.
